entries.reason: iOS 6 already carries JavaScriptCore.framework's C API - JSContextGroupRef, JSGlobalContextRef, JSObjectRef and their functions, all confirmed present by coordination/corpus/caches/6.0.tsv, 93 JS-prefixed symbols, not by reading a running process's memory. The Objective-C API of iOS 7 is a wrapper over exactly that C API, so it is implemented rather than left absent
entries.effect: -init creates its own JSContextGroupRef, released on dealloc; -addManagedReference:withOwner: and -removeManagedReference:withOwner: report the graph as the release does: a managed value is kept while its owner is reachable from JavaScript, built as JavaScript objects the engine's own collector follows (JSVirtualMachine.m), since the iOS 6 C API has no hook into the collector; facts/JavaScriptCore/JSContext.md
entries.source: SDK 16.4, JavaScriptCore; coordination/corpus/caches/6.0.tsv for what iOS 6 exports

entries.reason: a wrapper over the JSGlobalContextRef and JSEvaluateScript the release already carries
entries.effect: -init, -initWithVirtualMachine:, -evaluateScript: and -evaluateScript:withSourceURL: work as the header describes; +currentContext, +currentThis, +currentCallee and +currentArguments answer from inside a callback JavaScript makes into an exported block or JSExport method, and nil outside one; exception and exceptionHandler follow the header's own default (an uncaught exception is stored to exception); name is kept locally, since the release exports no JSGlobalContextSetName to show it anywhere; inspectable is stored and has no other effect, since there is no Web Inspector on this release to show it to; contextWithJSGlobalContextRef: and JSGlobalContextRef bridge to the C API, registering and finding wrappers by a global map keyed on the JSGlobalContextRef itself so the same context always returns the same Objective-C wrapper
entries.source: SDK 16.4, JavaScriptCore; coordination/corpus/caches/6.0.tsv for what iOS 6 exports

entries.reason: a wrapper over JSValueRef/JSObjectRef and the conversion table JSValue.h itself documents
entries.effect: every creation method, every to* and toObjectOfClass:, every is* type check, isEqualToObject:, isEqualWithTypeCoercionToObject:, isInstanceOf:, callWithArguments:, constructWithArguments:, invokeMethod:withArguments:, the property-access and subscript categories, the CGPoint/CGRect/CGSize/NSRange struct category and the C API bridging category are implemented. An Objective-C object that does not derive from NSString/NSNumber/NSDictionary/NSArray/NSDate/NSBlock and does not conform to a protocol incorporating JSExport becomes an opaque JavaScript wrapper object with no properties or methods, round-tripping back through toObject but nothing more; conversions follow the release's own walk - cycles and shared references, Date, null as NSNull, toArray/toDictionary of a primitive a TypeError to the handler, a throwing toString/valueOf to the handler; a block's or JSExport method's object arguments are converted by their declared class (the block's signature read per the documented clang Block ABI); blocks are called through NSInvocation as the release calls them, C numbers, bool and CGPoint/CGSize/CGRect/NSRange arguments and returns converted as the release converts them, and a block is a Function to script, new included; isArray, isDate and toObject tell arrays and Dates by the object's own class, asked of the virtual machine's own context, rather than the C API's JSValueIsArray and JSValueIsDate, which the release does not export and this port now carries over the same helper (registry/JavaScriptCore/capi.json, facts/JavaScriptCore/CAPI.md); promises are carried as the engine's own ES5 script with the job queue drained when the outermost call into JavaScript returns (on the next run loop turn under script run through the C API directly), and valueWithNewPromiseResolvedWithResult:nil and ...RejectedWithReason:nil raise NSInvalidArgumentException as the release does; the 2012 engine has no symbols, so valueWithNewSymbolFromDescription: notes a TypeError on the context and answers undefined and isSymbol answers NO; device-unverified; facts/JavaScriptCore/JSContext.md
entries.source: SDK 16.4, JavaScriptCore; coordination/corpus/caches/6.0.tsv for what iOS 6 exports

entries.reason: the real class exists to avoid a retain cycle when a JSValue is stored on an object exported to JavaScript; this port keeps that contract without the collector the real one relies on
entries.effect: managedValueWithValue:, managedValueWithValue:andOwner:, initWithValue: and value are implemented; the JavaScript value itself is held GC-weakly through the release's JSWeakObjectMap (exported by 6.0, private header), primitives and strings by value, and reads back nil once the collector has taken it; facts/JavaScriptCore/JSContext.md
